newsitem.title: GHANA: ECOWAS talks tough on Sierra Leone as 15 more die.
newsitem.headline: ECOWAS talks tough on Sierra Leone as 15 more die.

text.p: Foreign ministers from four West African states threatened tougher sanctions on Sierra Leone's military junta on Friday after fighting between the two sides killed another 15 people around the country's main airport.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has already imposed an air, land and sea blockade on Sierra Leone in an effort to force the junta to restore President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, ousted on May 25.

An ECOWAS summit in Abuja, Nigeria, from August 27 to 29 will consider other measures, but Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi refused to elaborate at a news conference held after a two-day meeting in the Ghanaian capital, Accra.

Ikimi condemned the latest fighting between ECOWAS troops and junta forces which has killed 15 people, most of them civilians, in and around Lungi, near the capital Freetown and site of the country's international airport.
"It seems to be a pattern of the elements in Sierra Leone that any time talks are going on, they attack our men," Ikimi said.

Residents on Friday said there had been further heavy fighting around the airport town of Lungi overnight between Nigerian-led ECOMOG forces and Sierra Leone army troops, backed by RUF rebels who have rallied to the junta.

Sierra Leone army chiefs would not confirm the overnight fighting and maintained that their troops had pulled back from the airport area after being shelled by ECOMOG forces in the early hours of Thursday.
Sierra Leone chief of army staff Nelson Williams told reporters on Friday: "Our troops are now 2-1/2 miles from the airport."
On Thursday, Brigadier Samuel Koroma, brother of junta leader Johnny Paul Korona, said the Sierra Leone forces had withdrawn some 35 miles (some 20 km) from the airport.
However, a senior member of the junta, who requested anonymity, told Reuters: "We don't want the Nigerians at the airport. We will continue to harrass them to leave there."
The ECOMOG high command issued a statement late on Thursday accusing the junta troops of breaking the ceasefire and launching an attack on its soldiers on Wednesday night.
"(The junta) and its cohorts have violated the ceasefire by its unwholesome actions against ECOMOG troops and the innocent citizens of Sierra Leone," it said.
Ikimi said in Accra that the ECOWAS forces would not give up. "We have the backing of the international community. I hope they will give us the material support as well," he said.

He hinted that the ECOWAS ministers might consider releasing Foday Sankoh, leader of the RUF rebels, who is under effective house arrest in Nigeria. Junta leaders have demanded that he be freed to take part in peace talks.
He was not allowed to travel to Abidjan, Ivory Coast, for talks that collapsed last month after the junta said it intended to stay in power for four years.
The Accra meeting was attended by ministers from Ghana, Ivory Coast and Guinea as well as Nigeria. These four countries have been mandated by ECOWAS to find a solution to the Sierra Leone crisis.
